==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|sho͞ot}}:
** {{IPA|en|/ʃuːt/|a=RP}}
** {{IPA|en|/ʃʉwt/|a=SSB}}
*** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Back ache-shoot.wav|a=SSB}}
** {{IPA|en|/ʃut/|a=GA}}
*** {{audio|en|en-us-shoot.ogg|a=US}}
** {{IPA|en|/ʃʉːt/|a=AU!Australia,NZ}}
** {{IPA|en|/ʃʉt/|a=Scotland,NI}}
** {{IPA|en|/ʃɪʊt/|a=Wales}}
* {{rhymes|en|uːt|s=1}}
* {{homophones|en|chute}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=launch|:inh|enm:scheten<alt:schoten>|tree=1}}
{{inh+|en|enm|scheten,schoten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċēotan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skeutan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skeutaną}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro||*(s)kéwd-e-ti}}, thematic present of {{m|ine-pro|*(s)kewd-||to shoot, throw}}.

{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|fy|sjitte}}, {{cog|nds|scheten}}, {{cog|nl|schieten}}, {{cog|de|schießen}}, {{cog|da|skyde}}, {{cog|nb|skyte}}, {{cog|nn|skyta}}, {{cog|sv|skjuta}}; and also, through Indo-European, with {{cog|ru|кида́ть}}, {{cog|sq|hedh||to throw, toss}}, {{cog|fa|چست|tr=čost||quick, active}}, {{cog|lt|skudrùs}}.
{{col-bottom}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb|~s|~ing|shot|+,shotten<l:rare>}}

# To launch {{gloss|forcefully project}} (a projectile or similar object).
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[fire#Verb|fire]] (a [[weapon]] that releases a [[bullet]] or other [[projectile]]).
##: {{ux|en|to '''shoot''' a gun}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[fire#Verb|fire]] or [[launch]] (a projectile).
##: {{syn|en|loose|q1=of an arrow}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|act=I|scene=i|passage=If you please / To '''shoot''' an arrow that self way.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[fire#Verb|fire]] a [[projectile]] at (a person or target).
##: {{ux|en|The man, in a desperate bid for freedom, grabbed his gun and started '''shooting''' anyone he could.}}
##: {{ux|en|The hunter '''shot''' the deer to harvest its meat.}}
##* {{quote-video game|en|developer=w:BioWare|title={{w|Mass Effect (video game)|Mass Effect}}|location=Redwood City|publisher=Electronic Arts|year=2008|genre=[[science fiction|Science Fiction]]|system=PC|scene=Noveria|isbn=9780784546642|oclc=246633669|text=Shepard: She's surrounded by geth and pointing a gun at us. '''Shoot''' her!}}
##* {{quote-av|en|title={{w|Hannibal (TV series)|Hannibal}}|date=4 April 2013|season={{w|Hannibal season 1|1}}|number={{w|Apéritif (Hannibal)|1}}|role={{w|Will Graham (character)|Will Graham}}|actor=w:Hugh Dancy|passage=I '''shoot''' Mr. Marlow twice, severing jugulars and cartoids with near surgical precision. He will die watching me take what is his away from him. This is my design.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To cause a weapon to discharge a projectile; to use a [[gun]] or similar weapon.
##: {{ux|en|They '''shot''' at a target.}}
##: {{ux|en|He '''shoots''' better than he rides.}}
##: {{ux|en|The man, in a desperate bid for freedom, grabbed his gun and started '''shooting'''.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[hunt]] game with a [[gun]]; to go [[hunting]] for [[recreation]].
##: {{ux|en|They're coming to '''shoot''' with us on Sunday.}}
##* {{RQ:Buchan Watcher|passage=The place was called the House of More, and I had '''shot''' at it once or twice in recent years.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To hunt on (a piece of land) with a gun; to kill [[game]] in or on.
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To function as a weapon that launches a projectile.
##: {{ux|en|The gun '''shoots''' well.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive|gambling}} To [[throw]] [[dice]]; to [[roll]].
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1980|author=John Scarne|title=Scarne on Dice|page=275
|passage=Then, when it was his turn to '''shoot''', he reached out with a completely empty hand and caught the dice the stickman threw to him.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|slang}} To [[ejaculate]].
##: {{ux|en|After a very short time, he '''shot''' his load over the carpet.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive|colloquial|chiefly|imperative}} To [[begin]] to [[speak]].
##: {{ux|en|"Can I ask you a question?"   "'''Shoot.'''"}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1951|author={{w|John Wyndham}}|title={{w|The Day of the Triffids}}|publisher=Penguin Books|year_published=1954|location=Harmondsworth|page=92|passage="And now," I suggested, "I think it's about time we began to rough out a plan of campaign. Shall I throw around a few observations first?" {{...}} Josella blew out a feather of smoke and took a sip of her drink. Savouring the flavour, she said: "I wonder whether we shall ever taste fresh oranges again? Okay, '''shoot'''."}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|figurative}} To [[dismiss]], [[reject]], or [[do away with]].
##: {{ux|en|His idea was '''shot''' on sight.}}
## To photograph or film:
### {{lb|en|ambitransitive|analogous}} To [[photograph#Verb|photograph]].
###: {{ux|en|He '''shot''' the couple in a variety of poses.}}<!--direct object: subject-->
###: {{ux|en|He '''shot''' seventeen stills.}}<!-- direct object: picture-->
###: {{ux|en|We can't '''shoot''' until the lighting is better. ''(intransitive)''}}
### {{lb|en|ambitransitive|analogous|cinema|TV}} To [[film#Verb|film]].
###: {{ux|en|The film was mostly '''shot''' in France.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To push or thrust (a [[bolt]]) quickly; hence, to open (a [[lock]]); to [[unlock]].
##* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage=There was no answer, so I took the big key, rubbed some salad oil into the wards, and after one or two bad shots, for my hands were shaking, managed to fit it, and '''shoot''' the lock.}}
# To move or act quickly or suddenly.
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[move]] past very [[quickly]] and [[suddenly]].
##: {{ux|en|After an initial lag, the experimental group's scores '''shot''' past the control group's scores in the fourth week.}}
##: {{ux|en|[[as soon as|As soon as]] the dog appeared, the cat '''shot''' underneath the couch.}}
##* {{RQ:Dryden Aeneis|passage=There '''shot''' a streaming lamp along the sky.}}
##* {{RQ:Twain Huckleberry Finn|chapter=VII|passage=It didn't take me long to get there. I '''shot''' past the head at a ripping rate, the current was so swift, and then I got into the dead water and landed on the side towards the Illinois shore.}}
##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=VIII|passage=Now we plunged into a deep shade with the boughs lacing each other overhead, and crossed dainty, rustic bridges[...]: or anon we '''shot''' into a clearing, with a colored glimpse of the lake and its curving shore far below us.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To go over or pass quickly through.
##: {{ux|en|'''shoot''' the rapids}}
##* {{RQ:Dryden Aeneis|passage=She {{...}} '''shoots''' the Stygian sound.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2005|author=R. G. Crouch|title=The Coat: The Origin and Times of Doggett's Famous Wager|page=40
|passage=It was approaching the time when watermen would not '''shoot''' the bridge even without a passenger aboard.}}
## {{lb|en|surfing}} To ride a [[wave#Noun|wave]].
##* {{quote-av|en|year=1966|director={{w|Bruce Brown (director)|Bruce Brown}}|title={{w|The Endless Summer}}|text=One of the fishermen was really stoked. He was trying to '''shoot''' the shore break in his canoe.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To tip (something, especially [[coal]]) down a [[chute]].
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To penetrate with pain as if with a bullet; to [[stab]]; to cause a piercing sensation.
##: {{ux|en|a '''shooting''' pain in my leg}}
##* {{RQ:Addison Cato|37|passage=Thy words '''shoot''' through my heart.}}
## {{lb|en|obsolete|intransitive}} To feel a quick, darting pain; to throb in pain.
##* {{RQ:Herbert Temple|passage=These preachers make / His head to '''shoot''' and ache.}}
## {{lb|en|obsolete}} To change form suddenly; especially, to [[solidify]].
##* {{RQ:Bacon Sylva Sylvarum|passage=If the menstruum be overcharged, metals will '''shoot''' into crystals.}}
##* '''1802''', {{w|Thomas Jefferson}}, ''{{w|Notes on the State of Virginia}}'', Query VII.
## To send out or forth, especially with a rapid or sudden motion; to cast with the hand; to hurl; to discharge; to emit.
##* {{RQ:Beaumont Fletcher Comedies and Tragedies|title=The Coxcomb|passage=an honest weaver as ever '''shot''' shuttle}}
##* {{RQ:Macaulay History of England|chapter=III|passage=a pit into which the dead carts had nightly '''shot''' corpses by scores}}
## {{lb|en|informal|ditransitive}} To send (to someone).
##: {{ux|en|I'll '''shoot''' you an email with all the details}}
## {{lb|en|informal|intransitive}} To [[leave]]; to [[depart]].
##: {{ux|en|Is that the time already? I've got to '''shoot'''.}}
# {{lb|en|sport}} To act or achieve.
## {{lb|en|wrestling}} To [[lunge]].
## {{lb|en|professional wrestling}} To deviate from [[kayfabe]], either intentionally or accidentally; to actually connect with unchoreographed fighting blows and maneuvers, or speak one's mind (instead of an agreed script).
## To make (the stated score).
##: {{ux|en|In my round of golf yesterday I '''shot''' a 76.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive|colloquial}} To [[inject]] a [[drug]] (such as [[heroin]]) [[intravenously]].
#: {{syn|en|fix|id=inject}}
# To develop, move forward.
## To [[germinate]]; to bud; to [[sprout#Verb|sprout]].
##* {{RQ:Bacon Sylva Sylvarum|passage=Onions, as they hang, will '''shoot''' forth.}}
##* {{RQ:Dryden Georgics|passage=But the wild olive '''shoots''', and shades the ungrateful plain.}}
## To grow; to advance.
##: {{ux|en|to '''shoot''' up rapidly}}
##* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=V|passage=Well '''shot''' in years he seemed.}}
##* {{RQ:Thomson Spring|year=1768|passage=Delightful task! to rear the tender thought, / To teach the young idea how to '''shoot'''.}}
## {{lb|en|nautical}} To move ahead by force of momentum, as a sailing vessel when the helm is put hard [[alee]].
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To travel or ride on (breaking waves) towards the shore.
##* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage=`Take the tiller, Mahomed!' I roared in Arabic. `We must try and '''shoot''' them.' At the same moment I seized an oar, and got it out, motioning to Job to do likewise.}}
## To push or thrust forward; to project; to protrude; often with ''out''.
##: {{ux|en|A plant '''shoots''' out a bud.}}
##* {{RQ:King James Version|Psalms|22|7|passage=They '''shoot''' out the lip, they shake the head.}}
##* {{RQ:Dryden Virgil|Pastoral 3|passage=Beware the secret snake that '''shoots''' a sting.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[protrude]]; to [[jut]]; to project; to extend.
#: {{ux|en|The land '''shoots''' into a promontory.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=w:Oliver Wainwright|title=Super-tall, super-skinny, super-expensive: the ‘pencil towers’ of New York’s super-rich|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20201005122034/https://www.theguardian.com/cities/2019/feb/05/super-tall-super-skinny-super-expensive-the-pencil-towers-of-new-yorks-super-rich|archivedate=5 October 2020|date=1 June 2019|passage=There is 432 Park Avenue, a surreal square tube of white concrete that appears to '''shoot''' twice as high as anything around it, its endless Cartesian grid of windows framing worlds of solid marble bathtubs and climate-controlled wine cellars within.}}
#* {{RQ:Dickens Pickwick Papers|chapter=[https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Pickwick_Papers/Chapter_49 Chapter 49]|text=There '''shot''' up against the dark sky, tall, gaunt, straggling houses.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|carpentry}} To [[plane#Verb|plane]] straight; to fit by planing.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1677|author=w:Joseph Moxon|title=Mechanick Exercises: Or, The Doctrine of Handy-works
|passage=two Pieces of Wood are '''Shot''' (that is Plained) or else they are Pared [...] with a Pairing-chissel}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[variegate]] as if by sprinkling or intermingling; to color in spots or patches. {{n-g|(See {{w|Shot silk|shot silk}} on Wikipedia)}}
#* {{RQ:Tennyson Poems 1842|volume=I|poem=The Dying Swan|page=54|passage=The tangled water-courses slept, / '''Shot''' over with purple, and green, and yellow.}}
# {{lb|en|card games}} To [[shoot the moon]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|aviation}} To carry out, or attempt to carry out (an [[approach]] to an [[airport]] [[runway]]).
#: {{ux|en|He tried to '''shoot''' the visual approach to runway 12, but the visibility was too low.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|surveying}} To [[measure]] the [[distance]] and [[direction]] to (a point).
# To carry out a [[seismic]] [[survey]] with [[geophone]]s in an [[attempt]] to [[detect]] [[oil]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1986|author=United States. Congress. Senate. Committee on Energy and Natural Resources|title=Outer Continental Shelf Oil and Gas Moratoria: Hearing|page=438
|passage=Once the area is ready to "'''shoot'''," the seismic crew places geophones and cables along the line of the profile to be recorded.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[drink]] (a [[shot]] of an [[alcoholic]] [[beverage]]).

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# The emerging stem and [[embryonic]] leaves of a new [[plant]].
#* {{RQ:Evelyn Sylva
|passage=Prune off yet also superfluous branches, and '''shoots''' of this second spring.}}
# A [[photography]] session.
#* {{quote-book|en|author=Dave Barrack|title=Grrl Power|format=webcomic|date=9 July 2015|section=Grrl Power #334 – Make down|sectionurl=https://www.grrlpowercomic.com/archives/comic/grrl-power-334-make-down/|text="Hmm."  "Problem?"  "Arianna warned me this might be a challenging '''shoot'''.  I think she was worried about you being belligerent, but the real issue is turning out to be your specularity.  It looks like I'm taking pictures of a flashbang."}}
# An occasion on which [[firearm]]s are discharged, such as a [[hunt]] or shooting [[competition]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1955|year_published=1959|author=w:Ian Fleming|title={{w|Moonraker (novel)|Moonraker}}|volume=|location=London|publisher=Pan Books|chapter=Secret Paper-work|page=7|passage=The lift eased to a stop and as Bond stepped out into the drab Ministry-of-Works-green corridor and into the bustling world of girls carrying files, doors opening and shutting, and muted telephone bells, he emptied his mind of all thoughts of his '''shoot''' and prepared himself for the normal business of a routine day at Headquarters.}}
# {{lb|en|professional wrestling|slang}} An event that is [[unscripted]] or [[legitimate]].
# The act of shooting; the [[discharge]] of a [[missile]]; a [[shot]].<ref name=Webster/>
#* {{RQ:Bacon Sylva Sylvarum|passage=The Turkish bow giveth a very forcible '''shoot'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1612|author=w:Michael Drayton|title=w:Poly-Olbion
|passage=One underneath his horse to get a '''shoot''' doth stalk.}}
# A rush of water; a [[rapid]].
# {{lb|en|weaving}} A [[weft]] [[thread]] shot through the [[shed]] by the [[shuttle]]; a [[pick]].<ref name=Webster />
# A [[shoat]]; a young [[pig]].<ref name=Webster/>
# {{lb|en|mining}} A [[vein]] of [[ore]] running in the same general direction as the [[lode]].<ref name=Webster />
#*: In the western [[dike]] is a '''shoot''' about 4 feet in diameter carrying a considerable sprinkling of [[cassiterite]], ore which in quantity would undoubtedly be worth mining. The '''shoot''' contains a large amount of [[muscovite]] [[mica]] with [[quartz]] and very little or no [[feldspar]]...
# An inclined plane, either artificial or natural, down which timber, coal, ore, etc., are caused to slide; a [[chute]].<ref name=Webster>{{R:Webster 1913}}</ref>
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1891|author=New South Wales. Supreme Court|title=The New South Wales Law Reports|volume=12|page=238
|passage=That there was no evidence before the jury that at the time of the accident the timber '''shoot''' was worked by the defendant company.}}
# {{lb|en|card games}} The act of taking all point cards in one hand.
# A [[seismic]] [[survey]] carried out with [[geophone]]s in an attempt to detect [[oil]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1980|title=The Williston Basin, 1980|page=159
|passage=Once the last line of cable has been retrieved, there is little evidence that a '''shoot''' has been conducted.}}
